The scope comprises investigation, engineering assessment and design services for Masterfield Levees A, B and C within the Camden Local Government Area. The services include review of existing information and available flood modelling; site investigations and survey; geotechnical investigation and assessment; flood engineering assessment; development and comparative assessment of levee improvement options; and identification of a preferred solution. The scope also includes concept and detailed engineering design of the preferred solution, constructability and constraints assessment, identification of planning, environmental and approval requirements, Safety in Design assessment, cost estimating and consideration of future staging and delivery requirements. The Service Provider will support the NSW Governments strategic assessment process by undertaking ecological field surveys, data management, analysis and reporting to validate State Vegetation Type Mapping (SVTM) and assess vegetation condition across Regional Forest Agreement (RFA) subregions in New South Wales. The services comprise three phases: Phase 1 – Survey planning and logistics: Development of survey methodologies, planning of field activities, management of work health and safety requirements, land access arrangements, site identification and data collection protocols. Phase 2 – Field surveys, analysis and reporting: Delivery of vegetation integrity and rapid flora surveys by suitably qualified personnel; collection and management of field data; spatial and ecological analysis; validation and refinement of vegetation mapping; assessment of vegetation condition; and preparation of technical reports and datasets. Phase 3 – Response to feedback: Revision of reports and supporting information in response to stakeholder feedback on the Draft Strategic Assessment, including additional field surveys where required. The services also include documentation of evidence, assumptions and limitations; provision of project data and deliverables in editable electronic formats; and transfer of intellectual property and associated usage rights to the NSW Government in accordance with contractual requirements.

The rig-based completion program is expected to commence from March 2026 (exact timing to be confirmed pending availability of workover rig). The two-well completions program is estimated to take approximately 22 days in total for the campaign, with six (6) days per well and allowing for one inter-well move and initial campaign mobilisation and end of campaign demobilisation, which may require slickline services assistance to deploy/retrieve downhole slickline plug for packer setting and/or packer pressure testing. Once completions have been installed, a well test equipment package will be mobilised once workover rig is moved off well location and each well will be flow tested consecutively over April to June 2026. The well test approach will utilise an ESP to flow water to surface while monitoring of pressures and flow rates to establish reservoir characteristics (assuming no gas or hydrocarbons are present in the well stream). It is anticipated that each zone in the well may be selectively flow tested for up to 10 days each with an overall well test duration on each well of approximately ~30 days per well. Slickline services will be required throughout the well testing duration to open and/or close SSDs accordingly as required to flow test each zone of interest. Supplier is to provide all equipment, materials and personnel for the provision of services required to complete the wells with a design and operational plan as detailed in the Technical Scope.

GS LLS has carried out soil remediation across 35 hectares of degraded grassland within the DEOH. This work targeted both the physical and chemical properties of the soil (Refer to figure 1 for direct seeding mapping). The soil remediation addressed several known soil issues, including low carbon levels, low pH, reduced calcium, elevated magnesium and manganese and poor soil structure through various soil remediation actions and ameliorants. Following the completion of the soil remediation the 35 hectares was seeded with a sterile cover crop (rye corn) to protect the topsoil from erosion and weed invasion. The site will be ready for direct seeding with native groundcovers (this contract) before Spring 2026.

Concurrently, an ownership and management strategy will need to be developed to inform decisions and future ownership of the land. The Planning Proposal will be reliant on inputs from the master planning and urban design exercise and will draw on the community and stakeholder engagement undertaken through the process, with a focus on implementation. The future use of land will respond to complex flood risk, and a range of technical inputs covering land contamination, a land use needs analysis, changing infrastructure needs, economic, social, environmental and cultural analysis to inform decisions to create a more sustainable and resilient Lismore. The outcomes will result in substantial changes to Lismore, with significant areas of previously residential land being converted to other land uses and zones. The Lismore community is still recovering from the 2022 floods, and this project is an opportunity to develop a positive vision for the future through meaningful collaboration with the community and other stakeholders.

Prepare a Design Options Report for the works including preparation of at least two (2) concept design options. 5. Undertake a detail survey of the site to inform the detailed design. 6. Undertake geotechnical investigations including non-intrusive methods such as geophysical survey and ground penetrating radar (GPR). 7. Undertake soil sampling and testing (geotechnical and geochemical) of the nominated stockpiled borrow material from the Bobs Creek Quarry. 8. Prepare a Geotechnical Investigation Report that details the methodology, test results and findings from the geotechnical site investigations. 9. Undertake design development of remediation works to inform the development of a detailed design that is construct only except for the Southern waste rock cut quantities and fill for the open pits. 10. Prepare draft detailed design documentation drawings for a construct only contract. 11. Prepare Final Detailed Design Documentation of the preferred remediation option. 12. Prepare Issued For Construction (IFC) documentation of the preferred remediation option.

Proposals to commence the work at any time from 1 October 2025 until 30 April 2026 will be accepted. Both 12-hour and 24-hour operations will be considered. Final program scope is to be finalised, so there are three operational scenarios that may eventuate and Suppliers should factor into their commercial proposals as relevant. The completions program involves running completions to depths of 790 m to 2,000 m. The work is estimated to take approximately 28 days total for all three wells to be completed. This comprises 7 days per well operations time, time for two inter-well moves, initial campaign mobilisation and end of campaign demobilisation. Please note that this 28-day campaign assumes 24-hour operations and will be longer in the case of 12-hour operations. The total campaign length will also depend on the number of wells in which completions are installed. Supplier is to provide all equipment, materials and personnel for the provision of Workover Rig Services required to complete the wells with a design and operational plan as detailed in the Technical Scope. A mini camp (offices for rig and servcies crew, smoko/break shed and toilet facilities) on location must also be included as a part of the rig. The supplier is invited to provide a fully equipped main camp to accommodate rig and camp crew and up to fifteen (15) third-party personnel. Optionally, the supplier may also provide quotationfor the provision of cementing, slickline and tubular running/installation services.

NSWTA requires the development of comprehensive as-built documentation to accurately capture thecurrent state of the RADNET network environments. This documentation is critical to providing a clear andauthoritative baseline of the existing physical and logical architectures, including configurations,interdependencies, and operational procedures. Establishing this baseline will reduce the risk ofmisalignment, support effective environment management, and enable a smoother integration phase tomeet current and future service level agreements (SLAs).The engagement will also deliver a structured gap analysis, undertaken in consultation with NSWTAstakeholders, to identify and remediate discrepancies between existing documentation and the live networkenvironment across each data centre. The scope of work will focus on four key operational locations: CastleHill Data Centre and National Operations Centre, Silverwater Data Centre, Unanderra Data Centre, and theSydney Olympic Park National Operations Centre.
